names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 24 Μαΐου, «Άγιος Νικήτας ο Στυλίτης Πρεσλαβίας ο Θαυματουργός», with the rank words left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 24. мај ст. ст., „Преподобни Никита Столпник“ — Преподобни is the `venerable` inside the `venerable-martyr` this corpus puts in `types`, and it is the only word stripped. **Столпник is kept although `stylite` is in `types`**, and this entry is where the reading is plainest: „затвори се у један столп, због чега се и прозва Столпником“ — he was *called* the Stylite because of the pillar, so the word is the name he is known by and not a rank laid on him, exactly as „прозват је Дивногорац“ works for the other stylite of this same day. **Measured**: `foldchk.py` returns `NO FOLDER HOLDS THIS FORM` for «Никита Столпник», where a bare «Никита» would have folded onto the corpus’s other Nicetases for nothing. The Greek form on this folder, «Νικήτας», is the bare one.

The heading of the calendar’s name link 1618, «Никита Столпник, Переяславский, прп.», with the rank word «Столпник» and the rank abbreviation left off — «Столпник» being stylite, which BRIEF-RUSSIAN §6 maps to a `types` entry and not to a name. His own life page spells the city «Переславский» in its title and «Переяславский» in its running head, and the day line «Переяславльского»; the form follows the name link. `fk.mjs` returned NONE for it before the write.

death.note: Widened, not narrowed, because two books disagree by ten years. saint.gr gave 1196, which this folder held alone. Охридски пролог за 06.06.2026 (24. мај ст. ст.): „То се догодило 16. маја 1186. године“. The Prologue also gives the day, 16 May, which is eight days off the 24 May both calendars keep him on and is not the thirteen days of a style conversion; there is no field for a day of death and it stands in the prose.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 24 мая ст. ст. — «Прп. Никиты , столпника Переяславльского (1186).»

attestations.note: The identification is exact: the day line gives the pillar, the city and the year 1186 this folder’s interval opens at, and the folder’s Greek and Serbian rows keep him on the same Julian day. `dates` WAS NOT NARROWED: the folder carries «1186 or 1196», widened by an earlier reading rather than chosen, and the Russian gives the night of 24 мая 1186, which is this feast’s own night and the earlier of the two years. The question of which year is the author’s and the Russian’s preference is recorded here and in the life rather than written into the interval. HIS OWN PAGE LISTS A SECOND DAY: «Дни памяти: 23 мая (Ростов.) , 24 мая», the first marked by the calendar as the Rostov local day; it is not thirteen days from this one. One row per church is the schema, so it is recorded here and he does not render on it. `venerable-martyr` already stands and the Russian bears it out — «преподобный Никита и сам завершил жизнь мученической кончиной». What the Russian adds and the paragraph carries: the tax-gathering under Юрий Долгорукий’s moving of the town in 1152, the words of the prophet Исаия that struck him, the human head and hand and foot seen in the boiling pot, the three days confessing his sins at the monastery gate and the finding of him lying in the marsh covered with insects, the hair shirt and the tonsure, the irons and the two wells and the round pit with the stone cap and the underground passage to the church, the kinsmen who took his crosses and irons for silver and killed him, the three beams of light over the Volga seen by the elder Симеон of the Yaroslavl house of Peter and Paul, the irons found floating and laid on his tomb, the attempt to open his relics under the metropolitan Фотий about 1420–1425 and the grave that closed itself, the side chapel of 1511–1522 and the akathist of the nineteenth century. azbyka.ru was not read.
Not checked: doxologia.ro's calendar for the same civil day (30 September 2026).

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 24ης Μαΐου — «Άγιος Νικήτας ο Στυλίτης Πρεσλαβίας ο Θαυματουργός»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 24 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. The page's head line reads «Αγιος Νικητας ο Στυλιτης Πρεσλαβιας ο Θαυματουργος (; - 1196)» and its body calls him «Ο Άγιος Οσιομάρτυρας Νικήτας», so `venerable-martyr` is the page's own rank for him; the day's line adds `Στυλίτης` and `Θαυματουργός`. The city the body names is Pereslavl, «στην πόλη Περεγιασλάβλ της Ρωσίας», and the monastery Pereslavl-Zalessky, which is why the English form says Pereslavl and not the line's `Πρεσλαβία`. The corpus keeps no Nicetas of this day. The page's closing dates are the relics' and not his: the chains thrown into the Volga, the three shafts of light the elder Symeon saw, and the opening of the tomb between 1420 and 1425 when the body was found incorrupt. The same page sends him to the synaxis of all the saints of Rostov and Yaroslavl, which is on 23 Μαΐου and which this run refuses as an unenumerable heading. No hymn.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 06.06.2026 (24. мај ст. ст.) — „Преподобни Никита Столпник“

attestations.note: The day’s third entry, on the same menologion 24/5 the Greek row already carries. The heading is quoted as the Prologue prints it, without a closing full stop, as all three of this day’s and all three of the 23 May’s do. **THE DEATH IS WIDENED BY TEN YEARS.** This folder holds `death` 1196 off saint.gr. The Prologue states **1186** — „То се догодило 16. маја 1186. године“ — so `death` becomes `earliest` 1186, `latest` 1196, display `1186 or 1196`, which holds both and chooses neither. **Nothing was narrowed**, and the ten years are well inside `date-audit`’s `wide` threshold. **A DAY OF DEATH, AND IT IS EIGHT DAYS OFF HIS FEAST.** „16. маја“ against the 24 May both calendars keep him on. **It is not the thirteen days of a style conversion** — that was the reading on 21 May in this wave, and it does not apply to eight — and **there is no field for a day of death**, so it stands in the prose as what the book says and nothing is moved. **AN IDENTITY REFUSED, AND IT IS THE SHARPEST ONE OF THE WAVE SO FAR.** „Тако исцели од узетости черниговског кнеза Михаила“ — so he healed the prince of Chernigov, Michael, of palsy. **The corpus keeps exactly one `michael-of-chernigov`**, the passion-bearer prince, and **this book itself keeps him on the Julian 20 September with a `venerated serbian` row already on his folder**, so the Prologue is speaking about a Michael of Chernigov somewhere in its own pages. **But that folder’s `death` is 1244 to 1246, `attested`, and this healing happened before a murder the same entry dates to 1186** — the man would have been an infant, if he was born at all. **Two commemorations on one calendar means two men, and this is the same test one step further out: a date that cannot hold one man means two men.** So **no `related` row is written in either direction, and the prince is named in the prose without a link**, which is what the floor test permits for a name no folder answers to. **This is a question for the author**: either the Prologue means a different prince Michael of Chernigov, or one of the two years is wrong, and nothing read for this corpus settles it. **New here, and it is the whole of his conversion**: that **as a youth he lived an unbridled and vicious life**; that **going into a church once by chance he heard the words of the prophet Isaiah, „Умијте се, (од греха) бићете чисти“ (Isaiah 1:16)**, which went deep into his heart and made a whole revolution in his life — **the same verse saint.gr quotes at greater length in Greek, so the two books agree on the hinge of his life**; that **he left his house, and his wife, and his property**, which saint.gr does not say and which makes him a married man; that he **laid chains upon himself and shut himself in a pillar, and was called the Stylite for it**; and that **after his death he appeared to a certain elder Symeon and ordered him to lay the chains, once found, in the grave beside his body**. **That last dovetails with saint.gr rather than contradicting it**: that page has the robbers throw the chains into the Volga and the devout old monk Symeon of the monastery of the Apostles Peter and Paul at Yaroslavl see three shafts of light above the river, after which the fathers carried the chains to his tomb — the Prologue supplies the command that sent them there. **Where it does differ**: the Prologue has the murderers take the chains **because, by their shining, they thought them silver**, where saint.gr has robbers who threw them away on finding them iron, and the Prologue makes the theft the motive of the murder itself. **Symeon the elder gains no row**: he is unidentifiable, the existing life already names him without owing one, and the Prologue adds no see, no date and no second name. `venerable-martyr`, `stylite`, `monk` and `wonderworker` are all four corroborated here and **no type was added**. No `locations`, although Pereyaslavl is named. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.

hymns.text: Православным смыслом юношеская возжеления возненавидев/ и доблественныя нравы восприим, врага победил еси,/ и во благоразумии Богу угодил еси,/ и свыше от Него прием дар чудес,/ бесы прогоняти, недуги исцеляти,/ Никито преславне,// моли Христа Бога, да спасет души наша.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 24 мая ст. ст., «Тропарь преподобного Никиты», глас 4 — proper to him, and it names him; the day prints no other Nicetas

english.text: With an Orthodox mind thou didst hate the desires of youth, and taking up a valiant manner of life thou didst overcome the enemy; in good understanding thou wast well-pleasing to God, and didst receive from him on high the gift of wonders, to drive out demons and to heal diseases. O most glorious Nicetas, pray thou to Christ God, that he may save our souls.

hymns.text: Христа ради от твоих рабов нуждную смерть претерпел еси/ и венец нетления от Него восприял еси,/ приходящим же с верою от честнаго твоего гроба подаеши цельбы,/ о Никито преподобне,// молитвинниче о душах наших.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 24 мая ст. ст., «Кондак преподобного Никиты», глас 8 — proper to him, and it names both him and the manner of his death the life gives

english.text: For Christ’s sake thou didst suffer a violent death at the hands of thine own servants, and didst receive from him the crown of incorruption; and from thy honoured tomb thou grantest healings to those who come with faith, O venerable Nicetas, intercessor for our souls.
